title: Voyager
note: Voyager 1 and 2 share one design. Frame (PDS host catalog): HGA boresight -z (dish faces Earth), science boom +y, RTG boom generally -y; the magnetometer boom is on the side opposite the science boom. Values marked 'NASA model' are measured from NASA 3D Resources 'Voyager Probe (B)' where no document gives them.

reference_model.note: NASA 3D Resources 'Voyager Probe (B)', 1.72 MB, ~20k tris, metres. Matches documents within ~4% on dish, bus and magnetometer boom; its two whip antennas are 4.69 m, documents say 10 m, so it shortens them.

hga_diameter.quote: A 3.66 m diameter parabolic high-gain antenna was mounted on top of the bus.
hga_diameter.also: Kohlhase & Penzo p.83 and PDS catalog round it to 3.7 m; NASA model 3.81 m.

bus_height.quote: a decahedral bus, 47 cm in height and 1.78 m across from flat to flat
bus_height.conflict: PDS catalog: 'about 2 meters in diameter and about 60 cm deep' (rounded; 2 m is likely across corners).

bus_across_corners.source: nssdca, derived: 1.78 m flat-to-flat / cos(18 deg) for a decagon

mag_boom_length.quote: The total interface-to-tip boom length is 13 meters. (section 5.2)
mag_boom_length.also: Astromast, 'highly rigid with respect to bending motions but soft to torsional'; NSSDCA: 'extending 13 m on the side opposite the science boom'; NASA model ~13.2 m.

whip_length.quote: Two 10 m whip antennas (used for the plasma wave and planetary radio astronomy investigations) also extended from the spacecraft, each perpendicular to the other.

science_boom_length.quote: a science boom extending out some 2.5 m from the spacecraft
science_boom_length.also: 'some 2.5 m' is approximate, hence 10%; NASA model scan side ~2.5 m.

rtg_diameter.quote: Each RTG unit, contained in a beryllium outer case, was 40.6 cm in diameter, 50.8 cm in length, and weighed 39 kg.
rtg_diameter.note: taken as the body (case) diameter: the NASA model's fins span 0.63 m around a ~0.45 m body, so 40.6 cm is not the fin span

rtg_length.quote: Each RTG unit, contained in a beryllium outer case, was 40.6 cm in diameter, 50.8 cm in length, and weighed 39 kg.

record_diameter.note: what shows on the bus is the record's aluminium cover (NSSDCA: 'encased in a protective aluminum jacket'); this is the Smithsonian's duplicate cover, transferred from NASA

also.quote: Each Voyager has mounted to one of the sides of the bus a 12-inch gold-plated copper disk.

record_depth.note: overall depth of the duplicate cover as catalogued; what the 1.3 cm includes is not stated (the page also lists 'Dimensions: 1/16 x 12in. (0.13 x 30.48cm)')

sources.quote: three Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs) mounted on a boom in the negative y-direction
mounted in tandem on a deployable boom

mag_sensor_positions.value: outer LFM at the tip; inner LFM at 0.57 of interface-to-tip (~7.4 m); two HFMs ~1 m apart on the boom support truss near the base

science_boom.value: scan platform at the end (ISS wide+narrow cameras, UVS, IRIS, PPS; 2 degrees of freedom); LECP, cosmic ray and plasma instruments inboard

low_gain_antenna.value: mounted on the HGA feed structure

record_cover.value: aluminium cover over the gold-plated copper record, gold coloured, with engraved instructions; mounted in plain view on a bus side

sources.quote: Each disk is encased in a protective aluminum jacket along with a cartridge and a needle.
Instructions explaining from where the spacecraft originated and how to play the disk are engraved onto the jacket.
The disc was mounted in plain view on the exterior of both Voyager spacecraft,
The golden records placed aboard Voyager 1 and 2 each have a cover with special etchings
A gold aluminum cover that protects the Voyager 1 and 2 gold-plated 'Sounds of Earth' records from micrometeorite damage.
sources.note: NASA GRIN caption as copied on Wikimedia Commons; the GRIN page itself was not reachable

record_engravings.value: record and stylus (upper left), video signal and raster (upper right), pulsar map (lower left), hydrogen atom (lower right), elevation view with binary playing time (middle left)

sources.quote: In the upper left-hand corner is an easily recognized drawing of the phonograph record and the stylus carried with it.
The drawing in the lower left-hand corner of the cover is the pulsar map previously sent as part of the plaques on Pioneers 10 and 11.

hga_depth.note: rim to vertex at our 3.66 m diameter, from the same fit (1.83^2 / (4 x 1.279)). Was 0.54 (rim 1.394 minus the hub's 0.854); the rim height stays within 3 cm of the old one. The NASA dish is 3.81 m across (rim at r 1.90-1.91 m).

mag_boom_elevation_deg.note: PCA of the outer boom only (y < -5 m, z > 2 m, 4482 points), NASA model. Earlier 43 deg was skewed by the RTG stack in the measured region

mag_boom_interface.note: 13 m (Behannon) back from the NASA model's boom tip (0.1, -12.7, 8.92) along that line; sits on the boom support truss

rtg_stack_inner_y.note: slices of the NASA model along y

rtg_stack_outer_y.note: slices of the NASA model along y

rtg_stack_droop_deg.note: slope of the slice centres from y -2.6 to -3.7, NASA model

rtg_stack_centre_z_at_inner.note: slice centre at y -2.6, NASA model

rtg_fin_span.note: x extent of the RTG slices, NASA model (body ~0.45 there)

feed_platform.note: region |x|,|y|<0.7, z>1.40 (above the dish rim), NASA model

feed_horn.note: region |x|,|y|<0.25 inside the dish, NASA model

mag_canister.note: estimated from the reference close-up; region box (0.58 x 1.17 x 0.99) also holds lattice

lfm_sensor.note: x extent at the tip and at 0.57 (0.25, 0.23), NASA model

whip_base_box.note: region around the whip root, NASA model

scan_platform_box.note: region y > 3.3, NASA model; lower 0.75 m full width, narrower above

science_boom_z.note: boom core at y 1.4, NASA model

under_bus_depth.note: estimated from the reference close-up (a strut frame under the bus); a region reaching z -1.17 also holds other parts

bus_z.note: z extent of the ten large side faces (normals every 36 deg from +x, 0.92-0.94 m from the axis), NASA model. Replaces frame_bus_top_z 0.604, which was the upper ring's base, not the bus top

bus_flat_azimuth_deg.note: side face normals at 0, 36, ... deg: a flat faces +x, NASA model

upper_ring.note: band of side faces 0.92 m from the axis between bus and dish, NASA model; an open band (no top): its upper edge meets the dish's back at r 0.92 and the dish's middle sits lower, inside it

hga_vertex_z.note: dish vertex height: least-squares paraboloid fitted to 662 rays cast down on the NASA model's reflector between r 0.5 and 1.85 m (vertex z 0.7116, focal length 1.279 m, rms 2.4 mm). Was 0.854, which was the hub under the dish, not the reflector.

record_centre.note: gold disc in the model's texture on the +x bus face, z -0.10..0.10, NASA model

record_texture.note: engraving layout: the public-domain redrawn cover diagram (Commons), each diagram group placed onto NASA's photo of the cover by tools/engraving.py fit (labels and arrows dropped); see the overlay check in the README

sources.quote: is in the public domain in the United States because it was solely created by NASA.
This file is in the public domain in the United States because it was solely created by NASA.

record_gold.note: linear RGB: mean of mid-brightness pixels (luminance 0.5-0.7) on NASA's cover photo, G/R 0.77 and B/R 0.09, scaled to R 0.85; film colour balance unknown

record_roughness.source: cover_photo, polished finish: mirror-like reflections of the room and hairline scratches
record_roughness.note: glTF roughness, judged by eye against the photo and chosen by the user on the home-page view (earlier 0.35); fully metallic

record_hub.note: eyelet at the centre of NASA's cover photo: ring ~42 px, hole ~20 px radius against the 1072 px rim radius (152 mm); height estimated, not documented

record_roll_deg.note: turns the texture upright (+z) on the +x face; the reference close-up shows the diagrams upright, record and stylus at upper left

open_questions: Scan platform size and layout: not found; would come from the NASA model and photos.
Surface finishes (gold/black blankets, bare metal): no document; photos needed.
Whip directions relative to the booms: PRA paper Fig. 5 text unreadable; needs a visual check.
RTG boom geometry, HGA depth, magnetometer boom angle and support truss: only from the NASA model.
MHW-RTG fin span: only from the NASA model (0.63 m).

Golden record cover: what the Smithsonian's 1.3 cm depth includes, engraving depth and method, hub height, and the exact turn on the bus are not documented; the gold finish method is not given by NASA.

budget.note: Raised from the 1.5 MB default (David, 2026-10-27, chose 'Raise to 2 MB') for the 2048 px baked colour atlas at JPEG quality 88.

sheet_frame.note: fixed framing shared by our sheet and the reference sheet, so the two overlay; union of both models' bounds

closeups.name: record
closeups.note: golden record cover on its bus face

bake.note: Base colour projected from NASA's 3D model (nasa_3d_voyager: one 1024 px photo-textured atlas, about 7.5 mm/px on the dish and 10 mm/px on the bus, so a 2048 px atlas holds all its detail). Two passes like Perseverance's: a near one, then a far one for stand-in faces the near pass misses. '_root' (a 24-vertex box with no material) is left out. No normal map: NASA's geometry adds little and the budget is 1.5 MB.
